correctness.rationale: The unit sphere is exhausted by smooth Euclidean arcs, interiors of taxicab segments and the four nonsmooth axis junctions. On a Euclidean arc, the unique norming functional forces the orthogonal direction and gives a contribution at most \(\sqrt2\). On a taxicab segment, the corresponding diagonal orthogonal direction again gives at most \(\sqrt2\). At \(x=(1,0)\), using the full support-functional interval reduces every admissible orthogonal unit vector to \(y=(a,\sqrt{1-a^2})\), \(0\le a\le1/\sqrt2\), with \(F(a)=\sqrt{2(1+a)}\) increasing and \(G(a)=1-a+\sqrt{1-a^2}\) decreasing. Their unique crossing is therefore the global axis maximum, and the substitution \(t=\sqrt{(1-a)/(1+a)}\) converts it to \(t^4+2t^3-1=0\). The positive-root monotonicity and independent algebraic elimination reproduce the stated exact constant and equivalent polynomial.
